title: My video on Duncan Sheik’s passing, for reference:  @Joe Weinberg  #m...
transcript: there's a manga musical by the late Duncan Sheik set in a French brothel and performed where Sleep No More used to be but unfortunately it misses the mark pretty catastrophically. Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen based on the 2013 manga of the same name by Moyoco Anno follows a sx worker played by Sophia Ann Caruso who's paid by one of her clients to chronicle her experiences. And yes it began previews mere days after Duncan Sheik suddenly passed away so it's uncomfortable to engage in criticism around it but I think we can all put our nuance hats on and remember that two things can be true at once: Sheik was a remarkable artist whose death is still keenly felt in the community AND this was probably the weakest work of his career. it doesn't erase the tragedy nor does it erase the brilliant work he's done in the past. and in fact it's because of my deep respect for him as an artist that I feel comfortable criticizing this Because I know that it won't be his lasting legacy. and he felt comfortable putting it out in the world; maybe he would have improved it through previews but honestly I think the problems ran too deep. superficially it still had that haunting, alluring Duncan Sheik sound and in some ways, even at his worst he's more interesting than a lot of musical theater writers at their best but underneath that style was a lot of fairly monotonous and uninspired songwriting and his lyrics were at the same time kind of flat in all the wrong places and jagged in all the wrong places so when I wasn't actively cringing I was kind of just checked out. which brings me to the story and I should give the disclaimer that I have not read the manga. so I don't know what carried over what was actively adapted by the book writer Leah Nanako Winkler vs. what was just lost in translation. but regardless what we ended up with did not work for me at all the intriguing premise is played out in what feels like the least interesting way possible focusing almost entirely on the deadbeat guy that the protagonist is delusionally hung up on which obviously does happen in real life but in this narrative context it felt stagnant and repetitive and the dialogue was just as cringey as the lyrics. The story is also punctuated by this roster of men coming into the brothel with these “outrageous” klnky fantasies but they're all based on some really simple iconography: a guy that pretends to be a dog a clown a bird a shepherd. again I'm sure these fantasies exist in real life but the way they're presented here felt like klnk Mad Libs sourced by the writers of iCarly and in fact, ironically, while the characters in the story have a very open, judgment-free attitude about it the direction and performances still plays them for laughs. Meanwhile the physical staging was pretty but felt like it was just kind of reheating the nachos of Moulin Rouge, Great Comet, the recent Cabaret revival. Sophia Ann Caruso is an undeniably talented actor and vocalist but struck me as kind of miscast here. so this was a misfire for me on pretty much every level. again all my love to Duncan Sheik. I stand by all the praise that I heaped on him in my retrospective obituary video. I think every artist deserves space for a flop or two this one was just very unfortunately timed
